source.O mapa de luzes noturnas do Earth Inform: The night-lights map from NASA's Earth Information Center, made with the Suomi NPP satellite, becomes music. For each year from 2012 to 2023, the lit area of the planet is measured pixel by pixel in this browser. At the end, the change map shows where there is more light (purple) and less light (orange).
source.Área acesa = pixels do quadro com luminâ: Lit area = frame pixels with luminance above 60 (out of 255), divided by the total pixels of the map. Growth compares the year shown with 2012. The change over the last year is the difference between two yearly frames, in percentage points of the map's area.
source.No mapa de mudança, roxo é onde há mais: In the change map, purple is where there is more light in 2023 than in 2012 and orange is where there is less. The ratio is the number of purple pixels divided by the number of orange ones.
source.Os instrumentos são sintetizados no nave: The instruments are synthesized in the browser: drums, metal instruments and strings are oscillators and noise, in rhythms inspired by the genres, played by the data. Underneath plays a recorded song, made with Suno, that you pick in "Background music" (by default, the genre's own), and the sounds generated by the event play on top; it follows the tempo of the data.
source.Os quadros vêm da visualização “Change i: The frames come from NASA's Earth Information Center visualization “Change in Night Lights between 2012 and 2023” (SVS 5313), made with Black Marble: yearly averages of night light from the VIIRS instrument on the Suomi NPP satellite. The original video is 7680 × 2160 pixels; here we use one frame per year, cropped into a 1600 × 900 world map, plus the change map.
source.A linha varre o mapa da esquerda para a: The line sweeps the map from left to right. Each column is a 3.75° slice of longitude: if it has lit places, a bell of the chord rings, higher the further north, and the sound comes from the side where the column is. The frames are visualization images, with brightness and colors adjusted to be seen, not calibrated radiance: the measurements are for comparing one year with another, not as physical values.

That is why the measurements are for comparing one year with another within the same set, not as physical values. A pixel counts as lit when its luminance exceeds 60 out of 255; in the change map, purple is more light in 2023 than in 2012 and orange is less light. Across the 12 frames the lit area goes from 0.315% to 0.447% (+42%), with a single drop, in 2020.
